text:
sarah: Heads up - spotted ~7 archived snapshots in prod that have no CMEK/cmek-id metadata after yesterday's deployment. No decrypt failures reported but metadata missing :eyes:

mike: which buckets/objects? any pattern on prefix or uploader svcacct?

sarah: all under gs://redwood-archives/region-eu/*/snap-*.tar.gz, timestamps ~2026-03-21 02:00-03:30 UTC. uploader service is backup-uploader@infra svcacct.

encops-bot: Alert: encryption-meta-missing detected for 7 objects in gs://redwood-archives/region-eu. Correlation id: a1b2c3d4.

james: quick guess: RBAC tweak yesterday touched backup-uploader bindings in infra-prod. @priya did a permission prune right?

priya: Yep, I removed a broad role binding in infra-prod to tighten least-priv. I replaced archive:admin -> archive:writer+kms:encrypt as scoped roles. I didn't expect metadata writes to be gated by a separate permission. Will check my diff.

mike: can we confirm if metadata was never written or stripped later? Any multipart uploads involved?

sarah: logs show multipart-complete events around the same window. Suspect finalization path sets metadata on CompleteMultipartUpload. If Complete failed to set cmek header we might end up with object without cmek label.

james: also check KMS grant TTLs. We had a rotation job that runs nightly and creates ephemeral grants for backup-uploader. If grant expired between complete and finalize it might have left object in limbo.

priya: pulling KMS audit now. One sec.

priya: KMS logs: two grants created for key projects/redwood/backups with grant-id g-9f3 and g-9f4 at 2026-03-21T01:50Z. Both show lastUseTimestamp 2026-03-21T01:55Z, then revoked at 02:05Z (manual prune by automation). That overlaps the window.

mike: that could explain race. If grant was revoked before multipart finalization metadata write, finalization may have fallen back to SSE-S or left header blank.

sarah: sample check command for object metadata (GCS):
```
gsutil ls -L gs://redwood-archives/region-eu/path/snap-20260321-0257.tar.gz
```
It shows: "Encryption: NONE" and no x-goog-meta-cmek-id.

mike: for S3-style example we used elsewhere:
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-archives --key region-eu/path/snap-20260321-0257.tar.gz
```
Look for ServerSideEncryption or SSEKMSKeyId.

oncall: Opening INC-2026-4389 to track. I'll start a quick scan to enumerate objects without CMek headers and list affected tenants.

oncall: scan in progress, currently 7 objects found, 3 are within retention window we can re-upload, 4 are older snapshots (need policy discussion).

alex: if objects lack CMEK metadata but are encrypted with provider-managed keys, they are still encrypted but not tied to our CMK - compliance flags this as non-compliant for some customers. Need classification.

priya: triage notes so far: 1) RBAC change removed a permission that allowed the uploader to write metadata key cmek-id. 2) Automation that prunes ephemeral KMS grants revoked grants during multipart finalization window. 3) Finalize path didn't fallback to atomic reattachment of cmek label.

mike: we should short-term: (A) patch automation to not revoke grant if there are in-flight multipart completions (B) rollback RBAC prune that removed metadata-write right (C) run integrity scan and re-encrypt or re-upload objects where possible.

sarah: + add to incident playbook: validate both object encryption headers and KMS grant TTLs after any RBAC or rotation change.

james: I can prepare a small script to re-copy objects preserving content and explicitly set CMEK label using the service's KMS client - will need a temporary grant for that job.

mike: example re-copy for GCS (uses Cloud KMS CMEK binding):
```
gsutil cp -n gs://redwood-archives/region-eu/path/snap-20260321-0257.tar.gz gs://redwood-archives/region-eu/path/tmp-rewrite && \
 gsutil rewrite -k projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/backups/cryptoKeys/cmek-key gs://redwood-archives/region-eu/path/tmp-rewrite && \
 gsutil mv gs://redwood-archives/region-eu/path/tmp-rewrite gs://redwood-archives/region-eu/path/snap-20260321-0257.tar.gz
```
Note: need rewrite permission and KMS encrypt permission for cmek-key.

priya: I'll temporarily grant rewrite/encrypt to a one-off job principal and log the grant with long TTL just for the fix. Will remove after.

oncall: customers? any exposed PII?

sarah: content still encrypted by provider keys, no plaintext exposure. Compliance impact: some tenants requested CMEK; we'll notify them and offer re-encryption where applicable.

alex: postmortem items: add CI gate to validate object metadata for archive path on deploys that touch uploader or KMS IAM. Also add telemetry alert when X% of archived objects in a day have missing cmek-id.

mike: quick mitigation patch: pin KMS grant prune automation to ignore grants for key backups/coral if there are active multipart ops in object-store. Filing followup PR.

priya: PR #4321 created to restore archive:metadata-write role for backup-uploader with least privileges.

james: script ready, running in staging now. Will run in prod once grant is in place.

oncall: INC-2026-4389 updated with remediation steps and estimated ETA 2026-03-21T12:00Z UTC for full cleanup.

sarah: thanks all. Can we also add a one-line step to run: 
```
python tools/check_archive_cmek.py --start 2026-03-21T00:00 --end 2026-03-22T00:00 --fixable-only 
```
and post results in the incident ticket?

priya: will do. Also scheduling a 15m postmortem sync in 30m to capture timeline and create playbook update.

alex: adding encops-runbook task: "validate cmek headers after upload and before deleting multipart temp parts".

sarah: final: follow-up PRs: #4321 (RBAC rollback scoped), #4323 (grant-prune guard), #4325 (CI metadata check). Assign owners: priya, mike, james. :lock: :white_check_mark:
